{
  "claim": "https://w3id.org/delphi/resource/claim/kimura-fixation-probability",
  "source": "network",
  "nanopubs": [
    "https://w3id.org/np/RA76F4g68zgxUhMgNanl8KsuUwKDJhYuUgXowdNzSsnMQ"
  ],
  "fields": {
    "rdf:type": [
      "https://w3id.org/delphi/ontology/Claim",
      "https://w3id.org/delphi/ontology/TestableHypothesis"
    ],
    "rdfs:label": "Kimura fixation probability of a mutant allele",
    "dct:description": "The probability that a mutant allele eventually fixes in a finite population depends on its initial frequency, its selective advantage and the effective population size, and equals its initial frequency when it is neutral.",
    "dct:source": "Motoo Kimura (1962) On the probability of fixation of mutant genes in a population",
    "delphi:context": "Assumptions: diffusion approximation to the Wright-Fisher model, genic (additive) selection with coefficient s, constant effective size N_e, no linkage to other selected sites. Formal status: proved within the diffusion limit.",
    "delphi:hypothesisType": "model-theorem",
    "delphi:proposedTest": "Track the fate of many marked mutations of measured fitness effect in replicate experimental populations of known N_e (e.g. barcoded microbial lineages) and compare fixation frequencies with u(p).",
    "skos:notation": "u(p) = \\frac{1-e^{-4N_e s p}}{1-e^{-4N_e s}}; neutral limit u(p) = p, so a new mutant fixes with probability 1/(2N)"
  },
  "assessments": []
}
